lines.text: A Tiffany bracelet landed in a kettle.
In December 2019, a woman dropped jewelry into a Salvation Army kettle.
lines.say: In December twenty nineteen, a woman dropped jewelry into a Salvation Army kettle.

lines.text: She said Merry Christmas and walked away.
The bell ringer called her a quiet spirit.
Inside was a yellow gold Tiffany bracelet and a ring.

lines.text: There was also a bracelet with diamonds and rubies.
A jeweler valued the Tiffany bracelet at 6,000 dollars.
lines.say: A jeweler valued the Tiffany bracelet at six thousand dollars.
It sold for fifteen hundred dollars.

lines.text: A captain said it shocked them to learn it was real.
That season, a kettle in Kentucky also received a gold bar.
Jewelry found in kettles is held for 30 days.

post.caption: A Tiffany bracelet landed in a kettle. In December 2019, a woman dropped jewelry into a Salvation Army kettle in Annapolis, Maryland. She said Merry Christmas and walked away. The bell ringer called her a quiet spirit. Inside were a yellow gold Tiffany bracelet and a ring, plus a bracelet with diamonds and rubies. A jeweler valued the Tiffany bracelet at 6,000 dollars, and it sold for 1,500 dollars. A captain said it shocked them to learn it was real. Jewelry found in kettles is held for 30 days. Photo: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA, CC BY 2.0.
